thread:
anya: Heads-up: i'm starting a focused cleanup for tool-calling docs. goal: one canonical Python + JS pair, small CI smoke tests, and a short migration note for legacy snippets.

ben: Nice. can you specify what "canonical" means? minimal surface area or full-featured?

anya: Minimal for quickstarts (5-10 lines) and a recommend-best (20-30 lines) that shows error handling, schema parse, and a mock tool run. both should demonstrate raw `tool_call` handling and the SDK helper parsing.

marta: For the mock tool run, can we keep it file-based? e.g., `docs/testdata/tool_call/mocks/echo_response.json` so both py and node can reuse.

chao: yes please. reuse is key. i'll add a tiny loader in the smoke harness to inject the fixture into the response object.

leo: CI concerns: flaky network calls are the usual pain. please ensure smoke tests never hit external endpoints. use local stubs only.

anya: Agreed. plan: dry-run env var for compile/render checks + stubbed e2e that injects `tool_call` payload from fixture. No network.

ben: Also add one example showing `arguments` encoded as a json-string vs already-parsed object. customers hit that often.

marta: Good call. i'll add two fixtures: `arguments_string.json` and `arguments_object.json`.

chao: small nit: show both `json.loads` and `try/except` in the py snippet so people see graceful fallback.

anya: Exact snippet sketch: \n```python\nresp = client.generate(...)
if resp.get('tool_call'):
    raw = resp['tool_call']['arguments']
    try:
        args = json.loads(raw)
    except (TypeError, json.JSONDecodeError):
        args = raw  # already-parsed
    print(args.get('result'))
```

leo: For node: short counterpart with `JSON.parse` + fallback to identity. also mention `--silent` flag to avoid CI noise.

ben: Migration note: we should add a short deprecation banner on old pages linking to canonical examples and include a dated timeline (90 days) + contact alias `#docs` for exceptions.

marta: i'll compile the legacy pages list and attach it to the PR. small suggestion: add a `redirects.yaml` in `docs/_data/` used by the site generator.

chao: CI job: `docs-smoke-toolcall` under docs workflow. ci-bot: please ensure the job runs with `timeout-minutes: 3`.

ci-bot: queued job: workflows/docs.yml -> docs-smoke-toolcall (expected 0.2m).

anya: i'll split this into three PRs: 1) fixtures + canonical snippets, 2) smoke CI job + harness, 3) redirects + deprecation banners. reviewers: @ben @marta for code, @leo for CI.

ben: i'll review PR #1 today. keep snippet length tight.

marta: PR #2: i'll add the GitHub Actions workflow entry and a small test runner script `docs/tools/smoke_runner.py`. does that directory exist?

anya: yes create under `docs/tools/`. keep runner idempotent and fast.

chao: tiny addition: include an FAQ blurb in the migration note about "why did my arguments arrive as a string" with examples of model outputs that trigger that.

leo: one more thing: add a signal in the SDK README pointing at "canonical tool-calling examples" so SDK consumers find them quickly.

anya: will do. timeline: PR #1 today, PR #2 tomorrow, PR #3 by end of week. target release next tuesday.

ben: thanks all. if anyone sees broken external references elsewhere, drop them into the PR description so we can include them in `redirects.yaml`.

marta: smoke job run: docs-smoke-toolcall (python) -> PASS (11s). ci-bot: workflow complete.

anya: great, opening PRs now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/3450 (snippets + fixtures)

chao: i'll start the Node snippets after PR #1 lands.
